subject: maths
title: Cross Product and Areas
welcome_lead: Forge new vectors and signed areas with the cross product.
meta_desc: HL Maths adventure on cross product, perpendicular vectors and parallelogram area.
final_note: a × b is perpendicular to both a and b!

concepts.def: a × b yields vector perpendicular to a and b.
Curl fingers from a to b, thumb is a × b.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Find vector perpendicular to (1, 0, 0) and (0, 1, 0).

Cross gives (0, 0, 1), the k-direction.

mcqs.q: What is the mode of the data set [1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 4, 5]?
options: The mode is 3 because it's the middle value.
The magnitude is 12 — you multiply the components.
Both 2 and 4 — the data set is bimodal because two values occur most frequently.
There is no mode because no single value is the most common.

mcqs.q: What is the magnitude of the vector (3, 4)?
options: The magnitude is 12 — you multiply the components.
Limits always equal zero unless the function is constant.
The magnitude is 7 — you add the components.

mcqs.q: Does the limit of f(x) as x approaches a have to equal f(a)?
options: The magnitude is 12 — you multiply the components.
No — the limit can exist even if f(a) is undefined or different from the limit.
The limit is always just the value of f at that point — that's how you compute it.
Limits always equal zero unless the function is constant.
